newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT-AUSTRALIA 10-YR BOND HUGGING THE TRENDLINE.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-AUSTRALIA 10-YR BOND HUGGING THE TRENDLINE.

text.p: *Australian bond futures contracts ended SYCOM with modest price gains in the face of a soft U.S. Treasury market with the 10-year bond holding on to a 4-1/2 month rising trendline.
*Comments by RBA governor Ian Macfarlane appeared to leave the door open for another cut in official rates.
Australian bond futures contracts ended SYCOM with modest price gains in the face of a soft U.S. Treasury market with the 10-year bond holding on to a 4-1/2 month rising trendline.
The contract ended after-hours trade at 93.220 compared with Tuesday's 93.205 close, although it failed to hold on to a session high of 93.335.

The bond still needs to maintain a foothold above 93.310 to turn around the recently vulnerable technical outlook, with the market having been tainted by continued weakness in U.S. Treasuries ahead of the retail sales report later on Wednesday.

The short-end of the curve ended with slightly larger price gains, albeit below the session's highs, following a less hawkish than expected speech by Reserve Bank governor Ian Macfarlane late on Tuesday.
Speaking in Perth, Macfarlane said the RBA did not have a growth ceiling and the economy could grow 4.5 percent or more over the next few years without sparking inflation.

"At the moment I do not see that monetary policy is placing any contraint on growth," Macfarlane said, saying the target made sure monetary policy was eased when the inflation forecast is below the target average.

The central bank governor also said it was entirely "fit and proper" that Australia should have a lower interest rate regime than the U.S, given that the two countries were at different positions in the economic cycle.
The December bill futures contract ended SYCOM three basis points higher at 95.07, equating to a cash rate of 4.93 percent compared with official 5.0 percent rates.
